messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: High GPU request queue growth in gcp-southamerica-east1 — autoscaler failing to provision. Paging oncall team now.

oncall-bot: details: queue_length=12k, avg_wait=18s, failed_scale_attempts=3, error=QUOTA_EXCEEDED

maria: on it. seeing rapid enqueue from batch inference jobs starting ~07:41 UTC.

sam: confirming: autoscaler logs show gce API returns 403 quotaExceeded for GPUs at 07:42:13.

jin: copying relevant log snippet: ```json
{
  "time":"2026-03-15T07:42:13Z",
  "service":"autoscaler",
  "msg":"createInstanceGroup failed",
  "error":"quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project redwood-prod in region southamerica-east1"
}
```

maria: thanks. is this a project-level quota or zone-level?

sam: it looks regional. cloud console shows GPUs used 98/98 for our project in southamerica-east1.

alex-cs: customer impact: some Hosted API customers on Dedicated fallbacks are seeing elevated 429s and higher latency for heavy batch jobs. CS is triaging any affected accounts.

jin: mitigation options: 1) re-route new batch traffic to us-central1 (capacity available) 2) evict noncritical warm pools in sa-east1 to free GPUs 3) request emergency quota increase (slow).

maria: immediate plan: (A) add routing rule to prefer us-central1 for new heavy batch jobs and canary slow-roll to avoid cold-start storms, (B) start evicting low-priority warm nodes in sa-east1.

sam: on (B) now — running eviction command to decommission warm pool nodes labeled warmpool=lowprio.

sam: command: ```bash
./infractl scale --region=southamerica-east1 --label=warmpool=lowprio --scale-to=0 --force
```

oncall-bot: note: evictions will increase cold starts for those workloads. set expected degradation note in the console.

maria: (A) updating routing policy: adding a temporary policy that routes model-heavy routes to us-central1 when queue_length>2000. Pushing config.

deploy-bot: config deploy started by maria at 07:49 UTC. CI checks passed.

maria: deployed. traffic should start shifting within ~30s. monitoring queue delta.

jin: monitoring: queue in sa-east1 dropping from 12k -> 8.3k in last 4 mins; us-central1 admitted ~3.5k. latency for shifted requests holding ~450ms.

alex-cs: heads-up: CS responded to two customers noting intermittent 429s — they've acknowledged and we gave ETA 30m.

sam: warmpool eviction freed 8 GPUs. autoscaler attempted 2 additional scale-ups and still hit quota for remaining needed GPUs. so eviction alone won't be enough.

maria: opened GCP quota request and escalation to support; ETA uncertain. raising priority with TAM.

jin: additional short-term step: enable model-variant fallback to 8-bit quantized variant for non-latency-sensitive batch jobs to reduce GPU per-replica memory and allow more replicas in remaining capacity. rolling variant config now.

maria: rolling quantized fallback for batch-route. will tag requests with X-Model-Variant until further notice.

oncall-bot: Reminder: runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-quota-exhaustion — follow postmortem checklist once stabilized.

sam: queue in sa-east1 at 07:56 UTC: 2.1k. us-central1 still absorbing. overall 429 rate down from 6.4% -> 1.1% in last 10m.

alex-cs: Customer impact update: 4 affected accounts, all on batch-heavy plans; one enterprise customer reported job timeouts — coordinated with solutions to retry/resubmit.

maria: current status: partial mitigation successful. still waiting on GCP quota increase for long-term. preparing incident summary for pager handoff in 30m.

jin: postmortem todo: examine why autoscaler didn't preemptively throttle or route earlier; add alert for regional GPU utilization >85% with proactive routing trigger.

alex-cs: I'll draft customer-facing note and coordinate follow-ups.

maria: oncall handoff: @sam will take next 2 hours to monitor; I'll write initial incident notes and start timeline.

sam: taking it. will monitor alerts and queue metrics.

oncall-bot: Incident: mitigated->monitoring. Priority: P1->P2. Handoff at 08:10 UTC.

maria: thanks team. closing live coordination thread. followup in #postmortems once we have timeline and root cause. :thumbsup:
